Maya: Heads up — after flipping the hybrid KV quant routing (INT8 primary, FP8 fallback) on the canary pool we see p50 decode latency +12% and a small but consistent perplexity bump on our smoke prompts. Memory per-GPU dropped ~18%.
Liam: when did the canary deploy go out? any deploy logs / commit?
Maya: deploy went at 2159876400, commit a1b2c3f. InfraBot posted the deploy in #eng-runtime: [deploy] canary/kv-quant-hybrid -> hostpool-2
Sanjay: do you have profiler traces? kernel switches around decode time could explain latency if we keep oscillating between INT8 and FP8 kernels.
Maya: attached small trace excerpt (copied below). note the kernel choice thrash at step ~38-46. Also saw two KV slab evictions coincident with client burst.
Maya: ```
# profiler snippet
step 36: kernel=int8_kv_gemm, exec_ms=1.8
step 37: kernel=int8_kv_gemm, exec_ms=1.9
step 38: kernel=fp8_kv_gemm, exec_ms=3.4  # fallback
step 39: kernel=int8_kv_gemm, exec_ms=2.0
step 40: kernel=fp8_kv_gemm, exec_ms=3.5
# kv cache
kv_hits=0.89, kv_evictions=2, kv_slab_util=0.72
```
Anya: interesting — that pattern looks like kernel hysteresis + calibration noise. INT8 quant stats borderline for some attention heads so the runtime flips to FP8 when certain per-layer scale quantizers exceed thresholds. Did you run calibration with the latest dynamic-range snapshot?
Maya: we used calib snapshot v2026-03-01. Re-running with the new snapshot from last night (v2026-03-16) gave fewer fallbacks in offline sims but the canary still shows occasional fallbacks under bursty input.
Liam: could batching heuristics be interacting? if a burst increases batching up to N, then kernel selection logic (which looks at sequence length distribution + batch size) might prefer FP8 for numerical stability at bigger effective matrix sizes.
Sanjay: yes — our kernel selector uses (batch_size * seq_len) heuristics plus layer-wise quant variance. Two mitigation ideas: 1) add a 100ms hysteresis window before switching kernel for the same request path, 2) tighten KV slab admission to avoid evictions that cause extra memory compaction work.
Anya: also worth checking whether KV cache float->quant conversion adds jitter. If we quantize on write and dequantize on read with slightly different scales under different mini-batches, the effective attention keys change and that can nudge the model out of its stable decode trajectory. That could explain the perplexity bump.
Maya: noted. I'll run a focused experiment: A) reproduce with fixed seed, single long stream (no batching) to isolate quant jitter; B) toggle hysteresis param kernel.switch_hysteresis_ms between 0/50/200; C) enable stable-scale mode (store per-key scale instead of global) and compare.
Liam: add measurements: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, kv_evictions, kernel_fallback_count, and a tiny eval set perplexity. Capture mem stats (cudaMemInfo) before/after.
Maya: will do. timeline: run experiments this afternoon, post results. If we can reduce fallback_count by >70% without losing the memory savings we're happy to roll.
InfraBot: canary deployment a1b2c3f monitored: CPU 18%, GPU mem avg 63%, fallback_count 14 (last 10m).
Sanjay: one more thought — try forcing INT8 kernel with a conservative clamp for a subset of layers (head layers) and see if quality holds. If so, we can opportunistically keep those layers INT8 and only fallback deeper.
Anya: agree. Also add a simple synthetic test that toggles batch shapes rapidly to stress kernel selector. That reproduces the thrash locally for me.
Maya: thanks. I'll post the experiment matrix + raw traces once done and propose a small runtime change (hysteresis + per-key-scale mode) if the numbers look good.
Liam: thanks Maya — ping if you want a hand with the profiling harness.
